item.title: Xinjiang scientific expedition finds "most resilient desert plant"
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
URUMQI, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- A type of moss discovered in a desert in northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region can survive conditions that would kill most plants, including severe dehydration, intense radiation, extreme cold and Mars-like space environments. This finding is among the major advances of the Third Xinjiang Scientific Expedition, which were released on Saturday in Urumqi, the regional capital city. Scientists describe the moss, Syntrichia caninervis, as "the most resilient desert plant found to date." The latest evidence of its remarkable resilience was uncovered in space. In March this year, the dried moss was carried aboard China's test cargo spacecraft Qingzhou for an orbital life-restart experiment. Facing microgravity and cosmic radiation, a controlled watering system gave the plants only a tiny amount of liquid water. Yet, the dried moss revived, changing from gray-black to yellow-green. "This is the first case in which a complete plant has been brought into low Earth orbit and successfully revived," said Li Xiaoshuang, a researcher at the Xinjiang Institute of Ecology and Geography under the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Continued in-orbit observation found the moss regenerating and thriving, indicating that it is an ideal material for deep-space life science research, Li added. In 2024, Li, as the first author, published the moss study in an academic journal, The Innovation, saying it is a promising pioneer plant for "colonizing extraterrestrial environments." Before the space test, scientists had already determined its genetic potential on Earth. Researchers of the Xinjiang scientific expedition discovered the plant in the Gurbantunggut Desert. After lab analysis, researchers found that the plant could tolerate the dehydration of more than 98 percent of its cells, survive rapid freezing at minus 196 degrees Celsius, and overcome strong gamma radiation. To understand how it endures such extremes, researchers obtained high-quality chromosome-level genetic information and found a large number of stress-related genes, unraveling the molecular code underlying this species' tolerance to extreme conditions. It can provide genetic material for improving crops and restoring desertified land, Li said. The Third Xinjiang Scientific Expedition was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Science and Technology. The previous two were conducted in the 1950s and 1980s, respectively. Over the past five years, the expedition team carried out studies on Xinjiang's ecology, land and agriculture, biodiversity and biological resources, mineral, energy and water resources. ■

item.title: 12 killed, 309 injured in attack on Riyadh airport as Houthis, Saudi Arabia trade strikes
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
RIYADH/SANAA, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- An attack targeting King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday afternoon has killed 12 people and injured 309 others, the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation said, as Yemen's Houthi group and Saudi Arabia continued exchanging strikes on major airports. The Saudi aviation authority said in a statement early Sunday that the fatalities included four Saudi citizens and eight foreign residents -- two Bangladeshis and one each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan. The injured are receiving treatment at several hospitals, with some in serious condition, the authority said. The authority said in an earlier statement that operations at the airport had been temporarily suspended pending damage assessments and safety checks. Following the Saturday attack, the Houthi group said in a statement that it was ready for reciprocal measures with Saudi Arabia to keep airports, seaports and other facilities with humanitarian functions outside the escalating military confrontation. Houthi-run al-Masirah TV reported Saturday that Saudi Arabia launched a new wave of air and missile strikes across Houthi-held areas in Yemen, targeting Sanaa International Airport in the Houthi-held capital, areas near the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait and several northern provinces. Also on Saturday, Yemen's government forces said that more than 1,150 Houthi fighters had been "neutralized" and over 180 military and logistical vehicles destroyed or damaged in over 1,900 strikes across multiple fronts in Yemen in the past 24 hours. The figures could not be independently verified. Around Yemen's southwestern city of Taiz, Houthi advances have put increasing pressure on government forces defending the city and disrupted key roads connecting it with government-held areas in southern Yemen, government military sources told Xinhua, adding that fierce clashes were underway south of the city. Supported by Saudi airstrikes, the Yemeni government launched a large-scale offensive on Monday, seeking to retake Houthi-held territory, with some of the fiercest fighting concentrated around the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. Yemen has been mired in conflict since late 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and much of the country's north. A Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015 in support of the internationally recognized Yemeni government, now based in the southern port city of Aden. The renewed fighting marked a major escalation after a UN-brokered truce in 2022 largely halted major hostilities. ■

item.title: Xinhua Commentary: Taiwan leader's repackaged rhetoric cannot conceal his secessionist agenda
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te reiterated his secessionist agenda and stoked cross-Strait tensions in a speech in Taipei on Saturday, using carefully crafted rhetoric to mislead the Taiwan public and sway international opinion. Once again, he invoked "democracy" to sensationalize the so-called "mainland threat" and promote a false narrative of "democracy versus authoritarianism." Such rhetoric seeks to exploit the concept of democracy to justify secessionism. The Taiwan question originated from a civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, while the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. Both history and reality make clear that Taiwan's future should be jointly decided by all Chinese people, including Taiwan compatriots. Differences in political systems are neither an obstacle to China's reunification nor an excuse for splitting the country. Lai said he would "never allow the distortion of World War II history." Yet his own words have repeatedly distorted history and undermined the outcomes of WWII. Lai refused to say a word about China's victory in the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the historical fact that Taiwan was restored to China after being freed from Japan's colonial rule. Instead, he has used the term "the end of the war," favored by Japanese right-wing forces, in place of references to Japan's defeat in the war. Lai's speech also contained statements that stoked confrontation across the Strait rather than promoting reconciliation. He pledged to continue military reforms, strengthen asymmetric warfare capabilities and increase military spending, while claiming that these measures were intended to deter war rather than provoke it. But such rhetoric cannot conceal his true colors as a saboteur of peace, a maker of crises and an instigator of war. The worsening of cross-Strait relations since the secessionist-minded Democratic Progressive Party came to power in 2016 demonstrates that secessionist moves in pursuit of "Taiwan independence" pose the greatest threat to peace and stability across the Strait. Since taking office, Lai has established a so-called Whole-of-Society Defense Resilience Committee, constantly conducted military exercises and civil-military integrated drills, designated numerous civilian facilities as purported wartime response centers, expanded military spending, and stepped up arms purchases from external sources. These moves have heightened cross-Strait tensions and exposed Taiwan to greater security risks. Lai's stubborn adherence to secessionism runs counter to the Taiwan people's aspirations for peace, development, and cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation. It also disregards the broader interests of the Chinese nation. No matter how he repackages his rhetoric or disguises his intentions, the secessionist agenda behind his words remains evident. Reunification is an inevitable historical trend. Attempts to pursue "Taiwan independence," including through military means, lead nowhere. People on both sides of the Taiwan Strait share fundamental interests in peace, stability and development. People in Taiwan should join their fellow Chinese on the mainland in opposing secessionism, upholding peace and stability across the Strait, and advancing the cause of national reunification. ■

item.title: China's trade strength rooted in competitiveness, not currency depreciation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- China has reaffirmed its stance on its foreign exchange policy amid increased discussions over the yuan's valuation, as solid facts and figures support the view that the country's export strength is rooted in its industrial competitiveness rather than currency valuation. China has neither the need nor the intention to gain trade advantages through currency devaluation, the People's Bank of China (PBOC) said in a policy statement released on Thursday, stressing that the country has never resorted to competitive devaluation. The statement came as some countries pointed to currency valuation as a cause of trade imbalances, thereby oversimplifying the dynamics between exchange rates and trade. The conventional view that currency appreciation weakens export competitiveness largely reflects a short-term and static perspective. Over a longer horizon, competitiveness is shaped by much more than exchange rates, analysts have said. This is particularly evident in China's case. The international competitiveness of Chinese products has at times continued to strengthen even as the RMB appreciated. From 2020 to 2021, the RMB appreciated by about 9 percent against the U.S. dollar, while China's share of global exports increased by 1.7 percentage points in this period, according to the PBOC. In 2022, by contrast, the RMB depreciated by more than 8 percent against the dollar, while China's share of global exports fell by 0.7 percentage points, PBOC said. These figures showed that China's imports and exports are relatively insensitive to exchange-rate movements, while neither its goods trade surplus nor its current-account surplus has a simple linear relationship with the RMB exchange rate, said Guan Tao, chief economist at Huafu Securities Co., Ltd. Attributing China's export strength primarily to currency depreciation or other purported factors including "overcapacity" reflects a fundamental misunderstanding of the sophistication and competitiveness of the country's industrial sector. At its core, China's trade growth is underpinned by its vast domestic market, comprehensive industrial and supply chains, well-developed infrastructure, abundant and highly skilled workforce, and steadily improving research and innovation capabilities, the central bank noted. Dong Ximiao, chief economist at China Merchants Union Consumer Finance, said that historically, the world's major trade surplus countries have generally been those with strong industrial competitiveness. For deficit economies, their deeper challenges lie in structural factors such as low savings rates, high consumption and insufficient industrial competitiveness, issues that cannot be resolved simply by focusing on the exchange rates of their trading partners. "Declining trade competitiveness in some countries reflects their own structural difficulties," said Hao Yubiao, director of the National Center for Economic Security Studies at Capital University of Economics and Business. "Pointing the finger at other countries' currency exchange rates amounts to avoiding the need for domestic adjustment and does little to solve the underlying problems." At a time when currencies in neighboring countries have been depreciating, China has refrained from pursuing beggar-thy-neighbor policies or competitive devaluation. This year, both the onshore and offshore RMB have strengthened past the 6.7 mark against the U.S. dollar. China had never resorted to competitive currency devaluation to boost exports to offset intensive external shocks in the past, the central bank said. Over the past two decades, the RMB has experienced multiple cycles of appreciation and depreciation, reflecting increasingly pronounced two-way movements and greater exchange-rate flexibility. The PBOC said that looking ahead, both appreciation and depreciation factors remain in play and that the future direction of the RMB exchange rates remains uncertain. Such two-way fluctuations are consistent with China's efforts to make the exchange rate more flexible and market-oriented. As a responsible major economy, China has also been committed to addressing such trade imbalances via international cooperation. At a meeting of G20 finance ministers and central bank governors last month, PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng said structural reforms are needed across economies to address global trade imbalances. He called on deficit economies to reduce fiscal deficits and raise domestic savings rates, while surplus economies should appropriately promote growth in consumption and investment. Countries should formulate medium- and long-term policy plans, make clear commitments and follow through on those commitments, Pan said. ■

item.title: Zheng reaches China Open final first time
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Zheng Qinwen hits a return during the women's singles semifinal between Zheng Qinwen of China and Elise Mertens of Belgium at 2026 China Open tennis tournament in Beijing, China, Oct. 10, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Chenlin) BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- China's Zheng Qinwen defeated Belgium's Elise Mertens 7-5, 6-2 here on Saturday to reach the China Open women's singles final for the first time, while home veteran Zhang Shuai and the Czech Republic's Katerina Siniakova advanced to the women's doubles final. Zheng, a wild card, broke 13th seed Mertens in the second game, but the Belgian broke back in the seventh to level at 4-4. After a tight finish to the opening set, Zheng prevailed 7-5 before taking control of the second to seal the victory. The result marked Zheng's best performance at the event and made her the first home player in tournament history to reach the singles final. "The best version of me will come in the future," reflected Zheng right after the match. "I spare no effort here (China Open). I will give it all out and present a good match tomorrow." Zheng will face this year's French Open champion Mirra Andreeva in Sunday's final after the fourth seed cruised past the Czech Republic's Nikola Bartunkova 6-2, 6-2 in the other semifinal. "I'm very happy and excited to be in the final," said Andreeva. "Obviously she (Zheng) is aggressive, she likes to hit a lot of balls, she tries to play fast. I will try to play my best in the final." In the women's doubles, top seeds Zhang and Siniakova defeated Indonesia's Aldila Sutjiadi and New Zealand's Erin Routliffe 6-4, 6-2 to reach the final. The women's singles and doubles finals are scheduled for Sunday. ■ Zheng Qinwen celebrates after the women's singles semifinal between Zheng Qinwen of China and Elise Mertens of Belgium at 2026 China Open tennis tournament in Beijing, China, Oct. 10, 2026. item.title: China, EU reaffirm stable, balanced ties as key trading partners: commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- China and the European Union (EU) have reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining stable and balanced trade ties as key trading partners after a meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism, an official with China's commerce ministry said Saturday. Chinese Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao and European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maros Sefcovic jointly chaired the second meeting of the consultation mechanism from Thursday to Friday in Beijing. The two sides confirmed that they would address trade and economic differences and each other's concerns in a balanced manner within the framework of World Trade Organization (WTO) rules, explore ways to deepen mutually beneficial cooperation, and promote balanced growth and further development in China-EU trade. Both sides agreed the consultation mechanism had been operating smoothly and efficiently, and that "the successful convening of its second meeting marked a new beginning rather than an end," said the official. The outcomes agreed upon at the meeting demonstrated that China and the EU had both the willingness and the wisdom to manage and properly resolve differences through dialogue and consultation, effectively preventing tensions from escalating, the official said. The two sides held intensive consultations in a spirit of mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit, discussing in depth ways to address each other's concerns on an equal footing, expand two-way market access and promote dynamic balance in China-EU trade, covering topics including medical devices, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, inverters, and agri-food products. According to the official, the two sides agreed to explore the possibility of reducing tariffs on certain goods within the framework of WTO rules, and hold a technical dialogue on the EU's Foreign Subsidies Regulation. In-depth discussions were also held on trade in electric and hybrid vehicles, which helped prevent further escalation, effectively safeguarded the actual export interests of Chinese companies and supported the stable development of China-EU trade in hybrid vehicles. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to addressing each other's concerns regarding export controls. The EU side will continue to work toward making progress in resolving key licensing cases involving China in the dual-use sector, said the official. They agreed that China and the EU have significant potential for cooperation in new energy, artificial intelligence, trade in services, the digital economy, and green and low-carbon development, and that they could further explore new opportunities and expand areas of cooperation. China will continue to welcome EU companies investing and doing business in China and to improve its business environment, said the official. China also expects the EU to provide Chinese companies with a fair, transparent and predictable business environment, effectively protect their legitimate rights and interests, and strengthen their confidence and expectations regarding investment and business operations in the EU. Looking ahead, the two sides will step up efforts on key trade and economic issues of mutual concern and work together to implement the outcomes and agreements reached at the meeting, said the official. They also agreed to hold the third meeting of the mechanism in March 2027. In the meantime, they will maintain close communication at all levels, including through a ministerial-level video conference next January. It was agreed that stable and healthy China-EU economic and trade relations serve their shared interests and also inject certainty and positive momentum into global economic growth and the stability of industrial and supply chains, said the official. ■

item.title: 90 years on, Long March spirit endures in China, resonates beyond borders
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
*The Long March spirit highlights the firm faith, strong will, and never-give-up attitude of the whole Party and all Chinese people to overcome major challenges during the revolutionary years. *In today's environment, people need to hold fast to the same values that made the Long March an epic undertaking in modern Chinese history, said Khairy Tourk, professor of economics at the Stuart School of Business at the Illinois Institute of Technology in Chicago. *The Long March is not only a towering monument in the development of the Chinese nation, but also a precious spiritual asset for all humanity in the pursuit of independence, freedom and liberation, said Etienne Bankuwiha, a Burundian sinologist. BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- This year marks the 105th founding anniversary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. The arduous journey, which lasted from 1934 to 1936, helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. Nearly a century later, the Long March remains an important window into China's history and development. "The Long March is like a spine of your body that goes right through the modern history of China," said Harold Weldon, an Australian publisher and filmmaker. For China watchers, understanding this pivotal chapter is essential to understanding the CPC's founding ideals and enduring mission, as well as the resilient spirit of the Chinese nation. GREAT TURNING POINT The victory of the Long March marked a great turning point for the CPC and the Chinese revolution, and stands as a towering monument in the historic process of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. During the epic military trek, the CPC-led Red Army broke through encirclement by Kuomintang forces. Red Army soldiers braved raging rivers, snow-covered mountains and treacherous grasslands, with some marching as far as 12,500 kilometers. "It was probably the greatest tale of human endurance in recorded history, I think, in terms of the hardships faced," said Weldon. The Long March is a classic example of the ability of the Chinese people to defy overwhelming odds, and is ready to put up with huge sacrifices in treasure and blood in order to achieve their goals, said Khairy Tourk, professor of economics at the Stuart School of Business at the Illinois Institute of Technology in Chicago, noting that "sacrifice is an essential part of achieving glorious victories." Paul Ilado, editorial director of Kenya's Radio Africa Group, said the Long March transformed a military retreat into a decisive political and historical turning point. The Red Army was under enormous pressure, he noted, and their ability to survive the encirclement campaign was crucial to the continuation of the movement. The historical significance of the Long March extends beyond military survival, Ilado said. As part of the CPC's revolutional legacy, he said, the Long March demonstrated that hardship had to be overcome, objectives pursued over the long term, and survival under extreme pressure sustained by organization and discipline. During the Long March, Red Army officers and soldiers were pushed to the extremes of their physical limits, turning this dramatic episode in world military history into a "glorious human miracle." The Long March spirit highlights the firm faith, strong will, and never-give-up attitude of the whole Party and all Chinese people to overcome major challenges during the revolutionary years. Wagner Lacerda Dantas, a Brazilian journalist with China International Communications Group, described the spirit as the determination to continue fighting for a collective goal even when circumstances appear almost impossible, bringing together conviction, courage, discipline, solidarity, sacrifice and confidence in victory. "What impressed me the most was the organizational cohesion and belief of the Red Army, although under extremely tough conditions," said Balew Demissie, senior consultant at the Policy Studies Institute of Ethiopia. When facing extreme natural environments such as snow-capped mountains and marshlands, as well as the chasing and interception by the enemy's materially superior forces, this army did not collapse, but instead demonstrated astonishing discipline and idealism, and ultimately achieved success, he added. Yuri Tavrovsky, head of the Expert Council of the Russian-Chinese Committee for Friendship, Peace and Development, likewise identifies endurance, sacrifice, patriotism and wisdom as qualities forged during the Long March. In his view, the experience helped shape a generation of leaders capable of confronting crises, assessing changing circumstances and finding a way forward. CONTEMPORARY ECHO The Long March belongs to a specific historical period, and China's circumstances today are vastly different from those of the 1930s, but foreign observers see its enduring relevance in the CPC's strong leadership and China's rapid development. In today's environment, people need to hold fast to the same values that made the Long March an epic undertaking in modern Chinese history, said Tourk, the economics professor at the Illinois Institute of Technology. "Without values such as sacrifice, patriotism, perseverance, and firmness, the people would lose their sense of direction," he said. "I believe that understanding the Long March is truly one of the best ways to understand how the Communist Party of China managed to grow under such adverse circumstances," said Dantas, the Brazilian journalist, adding that it demonstrated characteristics such as discipline, unity, organizational capacity, independence and autonomy, seeking truth from facts, and, above all, confidence in the masses. "The great strength of the Party during that period lay not only in its weapons, but in its ability to maintain close ties with the people," he said. Etienne Bankuwiha, a Burundian sinologist, said that amid life-and-death trials, Chinese Communists demonstrated unshakable ideals and convictions and made strategic choices decisive for the future of the Chinese revolution. "For China today, it remains a powerful source of motivation that encourages the people to overcome difficulties, advance Chinese modernization, and realize the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation," he added. During a visit to China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, Ilado, the editorial director of Kenya's Radio Africa Group, was struck by the transformation of land that had once been difficult to cultivate, which offered him a tangible way to think about the legacy of the Long March. "When I arrived in China and went to Ningxia, I was amazed at how a desert had been turned into productive land, and how today that area has become a breadbasket for the country and the world," he said. The connection, Ilado stressed, is the idea of undertaking a difficult journey over a long period without losing sight of the destination. A farmer cultivating difficult land, an engineer building irrigation infrastructure, a technician improving food processing or a young person leaving a poor rural community to pursue education may seem far removed from the Red Army of the 1930s, yet all can be understood through the determination to continue when the destination is still far away, Ilado noted. Joshua Kingdom, a research fellow at Uganda's Development Watch Center, sees the Long March spirit reflected in China's response to contemporary challenges. He said China's efforts to withstand external pressure demonstrated resilience and a determination to deepen cooperation with Global South economies rather than succumb to difficulties. BEYOND CHINA The significance of the Long March extends beyond the history of China. The Long March spirit of unwavering faith, perseverance and collective spirit transcends borders and ideologies, inspiring humanity to overcome adversity and strive for a brighter future. Demissie, the senior consultant at Ethiopia's Policy Studies Institute, said the success of the Long March contributed directly to the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. In his view, the independent and modern state that emerged from that history has since become an important force in promoting multipolarity, South-South cooperation and the rise of the Global South. The Long March is not only a towering monument in the development of the Chinese nation, but also a precious spiritual asset for all humanity in the pursuit of independence, freedom and liberation, said Etienne, the Burundian sinologist. "Seen from the broader perspective of the Global South, the Long March proves a compelling point: to achieve genuine liberation and prosperity, a country and its people must proceed from their own conditions, uphold independence and self-reliance, and defeat every obstacle through unity and struggle," he said. Dennis Munene, executive director of the China-Africa Center at the Africa Policy Institute, said the Long March spirit could encourage the international community to unite around common goals and pursue dialogue across civilizations to address conflicts, climate change and poverty. These challenges cannot be resolved overnight; they require sustained commitment, cooperation and a willingness to keep working despite setbacks, he added. Kingdom, the research fellow at Uganda's Development Watch Center, said that writings by people like Edgar Snow about the Long March have moved people across the globe, "because every individual, wherever they are living, they usually have fears to conquer." "So, I feel like when you have examples of people who have gone the extra mile to conquer different things that are really relatable in some sense, it moves people," he said. (Video reporters: Zhu Yinan, Chu Yi and Du Zheyu; Video editors: Wu You, Liu Xiaorui, Zhang Yueyuan, Wei Yin, Liang Wanshan and Wang Han)■
